newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French December bond futures rallied to set a new contract high of 126.18 after demand for long-dated bonds from investors triggered heavy buying in the futures market.
The December bond future settled at 126.14, its highest level this year, with a significant 163,228 contracts changing hands, while the benchmark 10-year yield fell to 5.95 percent.

French bonds outperformed German bonds all along the curve with the 10- and 30-year spreads straying further into negative territory. Two- and five-year BTANs also outperformed their German counterparts.
A trader at a large French brokerage said, "We've had very good cash buying by U.S. houses in the 10-,15- and 30-year area in France and Germany."
He said stops were triggered on the December bond contract first at 125.82/84, yesterday's closing area, and then again at 125.94.
A cash trader at a French bank said the buying started with bonds maturing in 2008 before moving to the 2012 and 2019 area of the curve and then there was some "very large buying of the 2023/2025s."
